findings.description: The 'data' bucket declares no ACL or public access block and is documented as public, so its objects (including customer-master.xlsx) can be read by anonymous internet users. No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined to prevent public ACLs or policies.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so sensitive customer data stored in this bucket is not encrypted with a KMS key under customer control.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this publicly readable bucket cannot be detected or investigated.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects deleted or overwritten by an attacker (or by ransomware) cannot be recovered; combined with force_destroy = true this removes any tamper protection.
A customer master data file is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which has no ACL restriction, no public access block, and no encryption, exposing PII to anonymous retrieval.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured for this bucket holding financial data, so access to it is not auditable.
Versioning is disabled and force_destroy is true, so accidental or malicious deletion of financial objects is irreversible.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later bucket policy or object ACL could expose financial data publicly without an account-level guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in the operations bucket are not encrypted with a managed KMS key.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit trail of read/write access to this bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket, so public ACLs or policies could later be applied unchecked.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its datasets are stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving no guardrail against future public ACLs or bucket policies.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The log archive bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or exfiltration of centralized logs would go unrecorded.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards the log bucket; because it uses the log-delivery-write ACL, an accidental public policy would expose the full access log history.

findings.issue_category: no enforcement of encryption in transit
findings.description: No bucket policy denies non-TLS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests on this or any other bucket in the file, so objects may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.
